## Overview

LRP77 is the gated [#104](https://github.com/dseinternational/language-reading-predictors/issues/104)
Phase-2 follow-up to the period-resolved gradient-boosting diagnostic
. Phase 1 found the
structure in the near-noise word-reading gain models sits on the **dose /
intervention-status axis**, with a weak positive dose signal that concentrates in
the on-treatment periods. This model quantifies that one signal with honest
uncertainty.

**Estimand.** Among children who were **receiving** the intervention, how does
word-reading *conditional change* relate to how many sessions they attended? The
outcome is the Beta-Binomial post-count of $W$ conditional on its own baseline
logit ($N = 79$) — conditional change, **not** a raw change score (Lord's paradox
/ regression to the mean). All three phase transitions (t1$\to$t2, t2$\to$t3,
t3$\to$t4) are stacked, and the model asks in addition whether that
attendance–gain slope **varies by period**.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\eta = {} & \alpha + \alpha_{\text{phase}[p]}
     + \theta_{\text{treated}}\,\mathbb{1}[\text{on intervention}]
     + \beta_{\text{arm,late}}\,G\,\mathbb{1}[p \ge 2] \\
    & + \gamma_{\text{own}}\,\text{logit}(W_{\text{pre}})
     + \gamma_A\,z(\text{age})
     + u_{\text{child}} \\
    & + \beta_{\text{between}}\,\bar{d}_{\text{child}}
     + \beta_{\text{dose}[p]}\,(d - \bar{d}_{\text{child}})
\end{aligned}
$$

with $\beta_{\text{dose}[p]} = \mu_{\text{dose}} + \sigma_{\text{dose}}\,z_p$
(partial-pooled period slopes) and $\alpha_{\text{phase}[1]} = 0$ (period 1 is the
reference, so the intercept design has full rank). Here $d$ is sessions attended,
**centred and standardised over the on-intervention rows only**, and set to zero
on rows with no intervention.

## Separating "was taught" from "attended more"

In period 1 every immediate-arm child attended 45–91 sessions and every
waiting-control child attended none: assigned arm and session count correlate at
**0.970**. A single dose coefficient spanning both groups is therefore not an
attendance effect at all — it is the randomised treatment contrast divided by the
mean session count. This model splits them:

- $\theta_{\text{treated}}$ — the **extensive margin**: on the intervention this
  period versus not. Read in period 1 this is a *randomised* contrast, and it is
  where this model's randomised evidence sits.
- $\beta_{\text{dose}[p]}$, $\beta_{\text{between}}$ — the **intensive margin**:
  attending more, among children already being taught. Observational.
- $\beta_{\text{arm,late}}$ — assigned arm from period 2 onward only, where both
  arms are on the intervention and arm reads as intervention **order**. In period
  1 it would be exactly collinear with $\theta_{\text{treated}}$.

The between/within split matters for the same reason. A single dose coefficient
sitting over a child random intercept returns a precision-weighted *blend* of
"children who attended more" and "periods when this child attended more"; the
random intercept does not make it a within-child quantity. $\beta_{\text{between}}$
takes each child's study-average attendance and $\beta_{\text{dose}[p]}$ their
deviation from it, so neither is folded into the other.

## Adjustment set (revised DAG)

The focal edge is $\text{sessions} \to \text{outcome}$. Sessions is the revised
DAG's `IS` node, and the per-period `attend` is the model's *exposure* —
regressing the outcome on it is the estimand, not an ITT-rule "conditioning on
`IS`" violation.

**The DAG does not give a clean back-door set here.** `IS` has three parents in
`dag/dag-language-reading.dagitty`: $A \to IS$, $GA \to IS$ and $IG \to IS$, and
all three also point into the outcomes. Age and assigned group are measured and
adjusted. **Latent general ability $GA$ is not**, and no measured baseline closes
it — Frank's 2012 caveat, that the children least able to learn tended to show the
poorest attendance, is exactly this path. Conditioning on baseline skills is a
*sensitivity* (see LRP77a), never a proof that the path is blocked.

- **$G$ — arm.** **Coding: $G = 2 - \text{group}$, so $G = 1$ is the
  immediate-intervention arm and $G = 0$ the waitlist control; positive =
  intervention benefit** (the `#117` sign convention). Enters from period 2 only,
  for the collinearity reason above.
- **$W_{\text{pre}}$ — not a confounder of attendance.** The autoregression / RTM
  control that makes this *conditional change*; parameterisation, not back-door
  blocking.
- **age — a genuine parent of both.** Adjusted linearly.

**Cumulative dose** (`attend_cumul`, the running sum of prior-period sessions) is
**not** conditioned on: it is a deterministic aggregate of the `IS` collider, so
adjusting it reopens the latent-general-ability back door and can bias the dose
slope and the arm terms (issue #269). It is available only as a flagged
**collider-sensitivity** option, never in the headline, and **is not fitted here**.

**Sample.** All gain rows with an observed outcome are kept. The waiting controls'
period-1 zero-session rows identify $\theta_{\text{treated}}$; they contribute
nothing to the dose terms, and the items-scale contrast is averaged over the
on-intervention rows only.

### Causal warrant and expectations

Every dose slope here is an **adjusted association**, not "dose drives gains" —
the corresponding randomised-arm result is the available-case modified ITT
estimate in `lrp-rli-itt-010`, with its stated missing-data qualification.
Phase-1 best strata reached only $R^2$ 0.1–0.3; the deliverable is a calibrated
attendance slope with credible intervals, not a strong predictor. Do not condition
on anything downstream of attendance.
